ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 10616, as amended), Articles 3, 3-2 and 5; Financial Intelligence Unit Regulations on Identification of Transactors; Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 29, 30, 48, 55 and 287-2 through 287-34 (Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company); Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended); Framework Act on National Taxes for corporate tax domicile and tax invoice requirements.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Registration (Legal Entity Existence and Registered Matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry Division of the relevant District Court of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: certified registry extract, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Route B for non-member states: certified registry extract, Korean notary public verification, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination embassy or consulate legalization. Routes are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, competent local tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: Business Registration Certificate, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Route B for non-member states: certificate, notary public verification, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination foreign mission legalization. Use only one authentication route based on destination membership; do not apostille and consular-legalize the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Approving Incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or sole incorporator of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: notarization by Korean notary public, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Route B for non-member states: notarization, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination embassy or consulate legalization. Parallel and exclusive; no sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and representative of Yuhan Hoesa, filed with the District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: certified registry copy, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Route B for non-member states: certified registry copy, notarization, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination consular legalization. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank licensed by the Financial Services Commission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Route A for Apostille Convention states: bank signatory confirmation before a Korean notary public, bank corporate seal attestation, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille. Route B for non-member states: notarized bank signatory confirmation, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination embassy or consulate legalization. Choose the single path required by the destination state; never chain apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory before incorporation: identify all shareholders, officers, beneficial owners at the 25% tier and any person controlling through nominee arrangements; screen every covered person and each counterparty, carrier, vessel owner, charterer and intermediary against OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated list, UK OFSI list, Korean Financial Services Commission designated persons, Interpol red notices and global PEP lists (heads of state, ministers, judges, military officers and their family and close associates); apply FATF-based risk scoring, enhanced due diligence for PEPs and non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, zero-tolerance positive-match policy, and report suspicious transactions to the Korean FIU and competent authorities as required; re-screen monthly and on any event-triggered change in ownership.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Internet Registry Office (IROS) commercial name search and electronic filing portal, supplemented by the National Tax Service Hometax business registration system for business registration number verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules, the primary legal name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be in Hangul script and must include the company-form designation Yuhan Hoesa. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) primary Hangul legal name; (2) phonetic English transliteration of the Hangul name; (3) registered English trade name; and (4) doing-business-as mark used for bank accounts, contracts and customs clearance. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name with the same business purpose, including logistics and transport activities under ISIC 5229.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Korea (if used as a state-implying token)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 30 days and cannot be extended; if the reserved name expires, a new reservation must be filed with a fresh search and fee. Upon any name rejection, the applicant or authorized counsel has 14 calendar days from receipt of the Registry Officer written decision to file a written objection with the Commercial Registry Division of the district court having jurisdiction over the intended registered office. The objection must attach the rejected registration, a revised Hangul name, phonetic English transliteration, business scope certificate and a legal opinion on non-confusing distinctiveness. If the registration judge rejects the objection, an immediate appeal may be lodged under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days, with renewed search and name reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The Commercial Act permits a mailing address to be used for registry filing, but for an OOG heavy project cargo logistics company the National Tax Service will generally reject a virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address for corporate tax domicile and electronic tax invoice registration. Banks will refuse a virtual office that lacks a physical lease, signboard, employee records and equipment for milestone-wire and letter-of-credit facilities. A physical commercial office is mandatory for operational substance; a virtual office is not recommended as the permanent principal place of business for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical lease agreement and deposit payment; (2) corporate bank statement within 3 months; (3) national pension, health insurance, employment insurance and industrial accident insurance records for at least one employed officer; (4) electronic tax invoice history; (5) fixed asset register for trucks, trailers and project cargo equipment; (6) customs broker agreements, bill of lading archives and cargo insurance; (7) registered signboard and actual reception. Quantified risk: approximately 35% for unannounced physical inspection by the district National Tax Service and municipal registry within the first 12 months, rising to 50% if the company invoices high-value cross-border project cargo without local staff or visible operating facility.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), specifically Articles 288-330 (incorporation and organization of a Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company), Articles 543-584 (corporate governance, board of directors, and statutory officers), and Article 289 (minimum capital provisions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (Court Registration Office) under the jurisdiction of the local District Court where the registered office is located, operating under the Ministry of Court Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jung-gwan) duly notarized, and the Certificate of Incorporation (Beop-in-deung-gi-bon-deung-bon) issued upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korea imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the total capital must be fully subscribed and paid in at incorporation, and the amount must be adequate for the intended business scope. There is no blocked escrow account requirement; capital may be deposited into a corporate bank account, and a certificate of deposit is required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF SOUTH KOREA, ARTICLE 368(4) AND ARTICLE 393. DATE: [DATE] PLACE: [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS] PRESENT: ALL DIRECTORS, NAMELY [DIRECTOR 1], [DIRECTOR 2], AND [DIRECTOR 3], CONSTITUTING A QUORUM. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Korea on [DATE] with a registered capital of [AMOUNT] KRW divided into [NUMBER] shares of no par value; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is authorized to manage the affairs of the Company and to take all actions necessary to commence business operations; WHEREAS, the Company intends to engage in the business of out-of-gauge (OOG) heavy industrial project cargo logistics, including transportation, handling, and warehousing of oversized and overweight cargo, as described in ISIC 5229; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board hereby confirms that the entire issued share capital of the Company has been fully subscribed and paid in by the shareholders as reflected in the register of members, and the Board ratifies the allotment of shares to the initial subscribers. The Board authorizes the issuance of share certificates to each shareholder evidencing their respective holdings. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby designates [BANK NAME] with branch at [ADDRESS] as the primary banking institution of the Company. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts, including operating, payroll, and escrow accounts, and appoints the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as joint signatories for all banking transactions, with the authority to execute any agreements, mandates, or instructions necessary for the operation of such accounts, subject to the Company's internal control policy requiring dual signatures for amounts exceeding KRW 50,000,000. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopts the registered office located at [FULL ADDRESS] as the Company's statutory seat and principal place of business. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute and file all necessary notices and registrations with the Court Registry Office and any other governmental authorities to formalize the registered office, and to lease or acquire the premises as required. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints [NAME] as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and [NAME] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until successors are duly elected. The Board authorizes the CEO to represent the Company in all matters, to execute contracts, and to delegate operational authority as necessary. The CFO is authorized to manage financial affairs, sign tax filings, and maintain accounting records in compliance with the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS). The Company Secretary is authorized to maintain statutory registers, minutes, and to ensure compliance with the Commercial Act. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to take all steps necessary to obtain all business licenses, permits, and registrations required for the Company's operations, including but not limited to the business registration certificate (Sae-roe-jang), logistics licenses, and environmental permits. The Board further authorizes the officers to engage external legal counsel, auditors, and consultants as needed. This resolution shall be effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of the Board of Directors. ADOPTED this [DATE] by unanimous written consent of all directors. SIGNED: [DIRECTOR 1] [DIRECTOR 2] [DIRECTOR 3]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registry Office (Online via IROS - Internet Registration Office System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the IROS portal to ensure the proposed company name 'Yuhan Hoesa' or any desired trade name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered entities. Submit a name reservation application online, providing the intended business purpose and the full name of the incorporator. The system will issue a name reservation certificate valid for 6 months. This step is critical to avoid rejection at the final registration stage. Ensure the name complies with the Commercial Act naming rules, including the mandatory suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa' for limited liability companies. If the name is unavailable, select an alternative and repeat the process.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of incorporator (passport or resident registration card)
Power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the system will provide reasons. File a new application with a modified name. If the rejection is based on similarity, provide evidence of distinctiveness or obtain a consent letter from the existing holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notarial Office) and Legal Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Korean attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation (Jung-gwan) in compliance with the Commercial Act. The Articles must include: company name, business purpose, registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, and the names of initial shareholders. The document must be signed by all incorporators and notarized by a Korean notary public. The notary will verify the identity of the signatories and the legality of the provisions. The notarized Articles are a prerequisite for registration. Ensure that the business purpose explicitly covers 'out-of-gauge heavy industrial project cargo logistics' and all ancillary activities. The Articles must be in Korean; an English translation may be prepared for internal use but is not legally binding.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, revise the Articles and re-submit. If the business purpose is deemed too broad or ambiguous, narrow it to specific logistics activities. If any incorporator fails to appear, obtain a notarized power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori) and the Company's Designated Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate bank account in the name of the company (or in the name of the incorporator on behalf of the company) and deposit the full subscribed capital. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (Capital Deposit Certificate) confirming the amount and the account holder. This certificate is required for registration. The deposit must be made before the registration application is filed. The bank will also verify the identity of the signatories and the source of funds for anti-money laundering compliance. After registration, the temporary account will be converted to a permanent corporate account. Ensure that the deposit is made in KRW and that the certificate is issued in the exact name of the company as per the Articles.
required_dossiers: Identification of the person making the deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the notarized Articles and a resolution of the incorporators. If the deposit is delayed, extend the timeline. If the bank rejects the account due to compliance concerns, provide source of funds documentation or choose another bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Registration with Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Deung-gi-so) having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for incorporation registration to the Court Registry Office. The application must include the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, name reservation certificate, and a registration application form (Form 1). The registration fee is paid via revenue stamps or online. The registry will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the registry will issue the Certificate of Incorporation (Deung-gi-wan) and assign a corporate registration number. This registration is the legal birth of the company. The process can be completed online via the IROS system or in person. After registration, the company must file for a business registration certificate (Saeup-jang) with the National Tax Service within 20 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, respond within the given deadline (usually 10 days) by providing additional documents or corrections. If the rejection is due to a defect in the Articles, amend and re-notarize. If the capital deposit certificate is insufficient, obtain a corrected one. If the registry requires a court order, seek legal counsel to expedite.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and Local Municipal Office (Gu-cheong)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 90 days of incorporation, file for a business registration certificate (Saeup-jang) with the local NTS office. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, and a business registration application form. The NTS will issue a business registration number (Saeup-ja-deung-rok-beon-ho) and a certificate. Simultaneously, apply for any industry-specific licenses, such as a logistics business license from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) if required for freight forwarding or heavy haul operations. For OOG project cargo, a license as a 'General Freight Forwarder' or 'International Freight Forwarder' may be needed. Also, register for value-added tax (VAT) and corporate tax. The business registration certificate is required to open permanent bank accounts and to issue invoices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the business registration due to incomplete documents, correct and re-submit. If the logistics license is delayed, apply for a temporary permit or seek administrative appeal. If the office lease is not finalized, provide a provisional address and update later.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (MOLIT) - Logistics Policy Division, and the local Municipal Office (Gu-cheong) for business operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Freight Forwarder License (Hwamul-un-song-ga-jang) and Heavy Cargo Transport Permit (Chung-ryang-hwamul-un-song-heo-ga)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) - Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Environmental Registration (for logistics and warehousing operations with minimal environmental footprint). However, if the project cargo operations involve temporary storage of hazardous materials or construction of heavy-duty infrastructure, a Full EIA Report may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Water Quality Conservation Act, with BOD levels below 10 mg/L and COD below 20 mg/L for industrial effluents. VOC emissions from vehicle and equipment operations must not exceed 100 ppm per hour. Hazardous waste handling must follow the Waste Management Act, with proper segregation, labeling, and disposal through licensed contractors. Noise levels at the boundary must not exceed 65 dB(A) during daytime and 55 dB(A) at night.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (So-bang-an-jeon-gi-hoe) from the National Fire Agency (NFA) for the registered office and any storage facilities, including installation of fire extinguishers, sprinklers, and emergency exits. Structural load inspection by the Korea Authority for Land and Infrastructure Safety (KALIS) for any heavy lifting equipment or storage racks. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including workplace safety training, personal protective equipment, and accident reporting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and entity registration are processed through the Hometax portal (www.hometax.go.kr), while export declarations are processed through Korea Customs Service via the UNI-PASS system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean LLC) with non-resident shareholders, the LLC itself is a Korean domestic taxable entity; the non-resident shareholders do not need a separate Korean tax ID solely for the corporate vehicle. The procedure is: (1) incorporate the Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act at the competent District Court Registry, with non-resident shareholders permitted to hold 100% of equity; (2) appoint a Korean resident statutory representative or domestic tax agent for service of process and NTS correspondence; (3) after commencement of business, file the business registration application with the competent local district tax office, either by visitation or electronically through Hometax using an authorized digital certificate; (4) attach the certificate of incorporation, court registration certificate, shareholder register, passport or ID of the statutory representative, Korean place-of-business lease or ownership evidence, and bank account confirmation; (5) the NTS assigns a ten-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which also functions as the VAT registration number. If the taxpayer is instead a foreign non-resident enterprise with no Korean incorporation but making taxable supplies in Korea, the foreign enterprise must appoint a tax representative and file a VAT registration application through the tax representative at the representative's local district tax office before the first taxable supply; no minimum turnover threshold applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification regime. A Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax and VAT; no hybrid mismatch or pass-through election is available for Korean tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No KRW turnover threshold applies to a Yuhan Hoesa LLC; VAT registration is mandatory upon commencement of taxable business activity. A foreign non-resident enterprise making taxable supplies in Korea must also register through a tax representative without any minimum turnover exemption. The simplified taxpayer regime is reserved for small individual business operators and is not available to a Korean LLC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporations in Korea are required to issue electronic tax invoices through the Hometax electronic tax invoice system or through NTS-certified EDI/ERP interfaces. The electronic tax invoice details must be transmitted to NTS by or before the day following issuance to support real-time matching against VAT returns and customs export data. There is no physical fiscal clearance device or digital stamp requirement in the Korean VAT system; anti-fraud control is achieved through mandatory electronic transmission, automated NTS data matching, and a statutory prohibition on issuing paper-only or fabricated tax invoices. A zero-rated export transaction must also be evidenced through the issuance of an electronic tax invoice referencing the export declaration or qualifying offshore service.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rating is available where the goods are actually exported from Korea pursuant to an export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS, title to the goods passes to the foreign customer, and the export proceeds are received in foreign exchange. For project cargo and heavy haul services within ISIC 5229, zero-rating applies when the services are ancillary to, or form part of, international transportation of goods, or when the services are supplied to a non-resident customer and are performed or used outside Korea. The taxpayer must maintain a clear commercial and documentary link between the service, the out-of-gauge project cargo movement, the foreign customer, and the receipt of foreign exchange.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration accepted and processed by Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic system for the relevant project cargo consignment
Ocean, multimodal, master, house, or through Bill of Lading, or Air Waybill as applicable, covering the out-of-gauge heavy haul movement from Korea
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the project cargo, size, weight, and the ISIC 5229 heavy haul handling services, cross-referenced to the export declaration
Foreign exchange settlement certificate or inward remittance receipt issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank confirming actual receipt of export sales proceeds in permitted foreign currency

If zero-rated export services are claimed, a written service contract with the non-resident customer demonstrating the international-transport or offshore-use nature of the project cargo haulage and handling services, together with a written performance statement confirming that the services were rendered in connection with international movement or used outside Korea

Transport and preventive survey documentation for out-of-gauge cargo, including route survey, axle-load validation, and heavy haul equipment statements, to support the connection between the project cargo and the zero-rated international logistics supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly audit zero-rated export claims by matching Hometax electronic tax invoices, UNI-PASS export declarations, bills of lading, freight forwarding contracts, and foreign exchange settlement records. If zero-rating is not substantiated, NTS assesses 10% output VAT on the gross export consideration, voids any refund claimed, and imposes statutory additional taxes and late-payment interest. Fraudulent or fabricated export documents, falsified bills of lading, or fake inward remittance receipts constitute tax evasion under the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act and may expose the company, its directors, and its statutory representative to imprisonment, monetary fines, and retrospective clawback of all zero-rating benefits for the applicable statutory assessment period.

stage_3.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify zero-rated export claims against UNI-PASS declarations, bills of lading, project contracts, and foreign exchange settlement records. If the supporting documentation is missing, incomplete, or inconsistent, NTS will disallow zero-rating, assess 10% VAT on the gross supply, and impose statutory additional tax and overdue interest. Fraudulent exports or fabricated export documents are treated as tax evasion under the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act, exposing the entity and responsible officers to criminal penalties, substantial fines, and retrospective clawback of every zero-rating or VAT refund benefit for the full statutory limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in conjunction with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance (MOSF) and the Foreign Exchange Information System under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised but tightly monitored current-account convertibility regime. The Korean won is freely convertible for bona fide trade transactions, but all cross-border movements are subject to reporting and validation through authorised foreign exchange banks and the Foreign Exchange Information System. Capital-account transactions, including the contribution of equity into the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, require an advance foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Once the investment capital is credited to a domestic foreign exchange bank, conversion from USD to KRW is permitted for the LLC's operational treasury. Profit and dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after payment of corporate income tax and withholding tax, with evidence of tax filing and audited financial statements. South Korea does not impose a mandatory export surrender ratio, but heavy-haul logistics providers must collect export proceeds within the statutory period and either deposit them into a domestic foreign-currency account or exchange them through a designated bank. All hedging and currency swap arrangements must have a demonstrated underlying commercial exposure; speculative forward trading by non-financial corporates is restricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from out-of-gauge project cargo logistics must be received within 18 months from the date of export declaration, unless a prior extension is approved by the competent authorities. The full amount must be paid to a Korean designated foreign exchange bank or deposited into a domestic foreign currency account. There is no mandatory percentage conversion into KRW; however, every collection must be reported under the Foreign Exchange Information System and reconciled to the related export declaration and bill of lading.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Foreign Currency Investment Account / Milestone Disbursement Operating Account
Capital Escrow Account / Trade Settlement FX Account
Foreign Enterprise Investment Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMI-only platforms are not a compliant substitute for a Korean corporate bank account. An unlicensed fintech EMI is legally barred from holding Korean won settlement accounts, executing FEIS duties, or performing foreign exchange bank functions. At most, such providers may offer front-end payment orchestration through a licensed Korean banking partner, but the underlying treasury rails and KYC responsibility must remain with the Tier-1 bank. The project cargo business should therefore direct all liquidity clearing, FX conversion, and trade settlements through domestic licensed banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean Tier-1 banks generally require the statutory signatory director to appear for an in-branch identity verification; remote consular proxy opening is infrequently accepted and only when the bank has an overseas branch/correspondent that performs a certified in-person interview. For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa LLC, at least one authorised director or a formally appointed local compliance agent must attend the onboarding interview, bring original passports notarised by a consulate, present apostilled company registration certificates, and submit a board resolution confirming signatories and operational authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cascaded foreign ownership with concealed ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) exceeding the reporting threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership ladder from the Yuhan Hoesa LLC up to every natural person; apostilled corporate registry and articles of incorporation; notarised passports of all UBOs; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations; parent company audited financial statements; and a sworn UBO declaration executed before a notary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and trade-control flags on OOG heavy-lift cargo, overweight road/rail permits, and possible military or dual-use end-use.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed cargo specification sheets; Incoterms; commercial invoice and contract; end-user certificate; end-use undertaking; export licensing assessment; UN/OFAC/EU sanctions screening results; vessel/voyage list; final delivery certificates; transport permits and customs declarations from Korea Customs Service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial transaction profile mismatches, such as immediate high-volume milestone wires to third-party logistics vendors that are not named in the original KYC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service contract with each vendor; board-approved counterparty list; milestone payment schedule; verification of actual delivery via POD/B/L and photographs for OOG moves; bank statement from a historical jurisdiction if available; and a cash-flow forecast with genuine project timelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or nominee management layers obscuring management control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid certificate of good standing; board resolution approving account signatories; notarised power of attorney or nominee declaration identifying the real principal; ID and proof of address for each director; criminal record certificates from country of residence; Korean tax registration and TIN; and any local supervisory filings certifying the entity's business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity for the Yuhan Hoesa LLC must be injected via a licensed bank in Korea after filing a foreign investment report with a designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remitting investor must send the capital via SWIFT MT103 from an account held in the legal entity's own name. The wire reference must include the Korean entity name and the foreign investment report number. The bank will credit the Capital Escrow Account and only enable KRW conversion after the FDI report is verified. A local certified public accountant must subsequently issue a capital verification report confirming the paid-in capital, to be filed with the tax authority and used for future profit remittances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for heavy-haul project cargo operations should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for operational charges and milestone payments, with clear reference to the underlying invoice and FEIS declaration. For high-value procurement or charter arrangements, irrevocable commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) and documentary collections are the preferred trade rails. Every outbound payment must be matched to a Korean customs declaration or service invoice, with the applicable foreign exchange purpose code reported through the issuing bank to the Foreign Exchange Information System.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts on USD/KRW limited to the documented amount and maturity of underlying project cargo receivables and payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/KRW with a licensed domestic dealer under an ISDA/CSA master agreement, used only for funding and project cash flow exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) matching the external debt facility notional, coupon, and maturity, with no speculative layer
FX options are not a standard corporate treasury rail unless separately approved as a prudent hedge of a secured bid or infrastructure project exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final corporate income tax return for the fiscal year, including reconciliation of financial statements to taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year companies; for non-calendar fiscal years, by the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a 20% negligence surcharge on unpaid corporate tax; underreporting attracts 10%, overstatement of refunds 40%; unpaid amounts accrue a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% until settled. Persistent nonpayment can lead to asset seizure, business tax registration closure, and criminal fines for wilful evasion. South Korea does not use an automatic annual administrative strike-off for tax delinquency; the equivalent remedy is compulsory business closure and court-ordered dissolution after prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (local income tax surtax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government taxation office of the city, county, or district where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 for calendar-year companies; within one month after the national corporate income tax return due date for non-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underreporting triggers a 20% negligence surcharge, with 40% for overstating refunds or tax credits, plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%. The local government may enforce by bank levy, real property seizure, or compulsory collection; prolonged default may cause business registration restrictions and tax licence closure.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% over KRW 300 billion; a 10% local income tax surcharge is separately added to the national corporate income tax liability.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises may obtain a 5-7 year corporate tax holiday and a 50% reduction for the following 3 years under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D and facility-investment credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law can lower the effective rate; OOG heavy project cargo logistics enjoys no sector-specific patent box, but free-zone logistics operators may access special tax support if designated as a foreign investment zone.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return for domestic corporations (NTS Form 105 series for domestic companies) filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal together with tax balance sheet, income statement and adjustment schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporations must also make semi-annual interim prepayment filings with payment of the prepaid corporate tax and local income tax; no quarterly instalment regime applies to corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and payment must be submitted within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end the filing deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Corporate entity classification and head office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies whether the taxpayer is a domestic corporation or foreign corporation, the head office address, business registration number and the fiscal year covered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'domestic corporation' for the Korean LLC; attach a schedule identifying every non-resident shareholder's country of residence, ownership ratio, tax reference number and DTA entitlement; failure to identify ultimate beneficial owners may trigger GAAR and treaty-benefit audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Business revenue and gross income computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records gross revenue from OOG heavy-haul logistics milestones, ocean and inland freight, demurrage, standby vessel charges, project cargo handling and mobilization fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate revenue from international carriage outside Korean waters and clearly source Korean domestic haulage and stevedoring activities; mis-sourcing cross-border project cargo revenue can understate Korean-source income and attract 40% fraud penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Non-deductible expenses and related-party adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reports book income adjustments for statutory disallowances, entertainment expense limits, excessive compensation and non-arm's-length international payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees, charter hire, intergroup insurance, equipment rental and interest paid to foreign related parties require arm's-length substantiation; excessive payments to a non-resident parent may be recharacterized as a deemed dividend subject to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Records the taxpayer's self-adjustment to the arm's length price on cross-border controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a transfer pricing discloser covering all international related-party transactions in OOG logistics; apply CUP or TNMM with a tested-party profit level indicator; NTS accepts a comparability range and may impose an adjustment plus penalties if the Korean LLC's margin falls outside the interquartile range.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims credit for foreign income taxes suffered on overseas project revenues and branch income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean LLC is taxed on worldwide income; claim the credit only for legally imposed foreign taxes, attaching country-by-country tax credit schedules and foreign tax assessment documents; uncredited residual foreign taxes are not deductible in Korea except where statute expressly allows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding tax on payments to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares dividends, interest, royalties, commissions and other Korean-source income paid to foreign persons during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each foreign payee and treaty base, certify the Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership statement on file, and confirm the exact DTA withholding rate applied; if treaty documentation is incomplete, the rate must be stepped back to 22%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return attracts an unfiled tax penalty of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under Article 47-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent under-reporting triggers a 40% penalty under Article 47-3; non-payment accrues daily late-payment surcharges under Article 47-5; criminal tax fraud under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act carries imprisonment up to 10 years where the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million and fines up to KRW 100 million.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate non-resident dividend withholding composed of 20% national corporate income tax and 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before paying a dividend, interest or royalty to a non-resident beneficial owner, the Korean LLC as withholding agent must obtain: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the resident country's tax authority; (ii) a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient has substance, control and use/possession of the income; and (iii) the treaty-relief application filed through HomeTax before remittance. If the full 22% is withheld, the foreign recipient may file a refund claim with the Korean National Tax Service within 3 years of the statutory filing date. LOB and Principal Purpose Test clauses will deny treaty relief to conduit or shell recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% on royalties and interest; under most Korean bilateral treaties the reduced rate is 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, with dividend treaties frequently allowing 10% or 15% depending on ownership thresholds and beneficial-ownership status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File are required when annual aggregate international related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Country-by-Country reporting notification applies to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance is strictly tested through the Korean GAAR, DTA Limitation-on-Benefits clauses, OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test and controlled foreign company rules; the OOG logistics company must demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea by keeping operational control, key personnel, heavy-haul contract execution, vessel/truck deployment decisions and asset management in Korea; a thin shell deriving logistics income for a foreign parent risks deemed-dividend treatment and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of milestone-based project cargo revenue, fabrication of subcontractor invoices, overstated foreign charter costs, or fraudulent classification of Korean haulage revenue as foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes applies a 40% fraudulent under-reporting penalty; Article 3 and Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act authorize criminal prosecution with imprisonment for up to 10 years and fines for tax fraud exceeding KRW 300 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced if the LLC is operated as a sham; directors are personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, penalties and daily surcharges; fraudulent asset transfers are recoverable in civil proceedings; the NTS can impose departure-restriction/travel-ban orders, and conviction leads to imprisonment, disqualification from serving as directors and personal asset seizure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Korean LLC with no substantive office, employees, bank account or operational contracts and using it solely as a routing vehicle to funnel heavy-haul freight profits to a tax-haven related party while claiming reduced DTA withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Principal Purpose Test and LOB articles in Korean tax treaties permit full denial of treaty benefits; the Korean GAAR allows reassessment at the full 22% withholding rate plus a 40% fraud penalty; false treaty-benefit certifications are independently punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Act on Regulation of Tax Evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign treaty-certification documents knowing the Korean entity lacks beneficial ownership are personally liable for the withheld taxes, expose themselves to criminal prosecution for false certification, personal asset restitution, travel restrictions and cross-border extradition under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Misdeclared Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare the Local File / Master File when related-party international transactions exceed KRW 10 billion, or recording management fees, charter hire and intercompany financing at non-arm's-length rates without any comparability analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Adjustment of International Taxes Act authorizes reassessment using the NTS's own benchmark, disallowance of the taxpayer's self-selected method, a 20% under-reporting penalty under Article 47-3 of the Framework Act and daily late-payment surcharges; persistent non-production of documents can lead to criminal prosecution for obstruction of tax audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve false intercompany pricing or withhold required documentation can be assessed personally where the corporate structure is used to avoid collection; the NTS may seize personal assets, impose departure restrictions, and courts may impose imprisonment for willful intent to evade international tax obligations.
